architectural_implications.after: A personal agent holds the durable context and dispatches to apps/tools as subordinate capabilities.
architectural_implications.before: Each app owns its own user state and UI; integration happens through the user manually moving between apps.
architectural_implications.consequence: Memory/context becomes the portability battleground; teams need export, ACL, and provenance primitives at the agent layer, and apps lose direct user lock-in.
architectural_implications.observation: Context ownership moves from the application to an agent layer that mediates all tool calls.

architectural_implications.after: Agent quality is a function of a maintained, permissioned organizational index with freshness and attribution.
architectural_implications.before: Agent quality is tuned at prompt and model level with whatever context fits in one request.
architectural_implications.consequence: Ingestion pipelines, per-document ACL enforcement at retrieval time, staleness detection, and citation of source become first-class production concerns.
architectural_implications.observation: Internal agents are grounded in an organization-wide corpus ("company brain") rather than a per-request prompt.

architectural_implications.after: Human points the agent at a large corpus; the agent fans out extraction and aggregates themes.
architectural_implications.before: Human asks a question, reads an answer, asks again.
architectural_implications.consequence: Harness needs checkpointed intermediate artifacts, cost/context budgeting, and spot-check tooling because errors are silent and occur at scale rather than being caught mid-conversation.
architectural_implications.observation: Work shifts from interactive chat turns to long-context batch extraction jobs.

architectural_implications.after: Agents act on the user's behalf without per-action confirmation.
architectural_implications.before: Human reviews each agent output before it takes effect.
architectural_implications.consequence: Design pressure shifts to capability scoping, action budgets, and reversibility of side effects; approval gates become exceptions rather than the norm.
architectural_implications.observation: Autonomous execution is projected as the default mode within 2-3 years.

article_ideas.angle: Translate the self-preferencing argument from antitrust history into concrete agent-layer architecture decisions, and name the specific primitives (routing overrides, permission precedence, context export) that determine whether the ecosystem stays open.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, agent-infrastructure founders, and product leads choosing where to build defensively
article_ideas.thesis: The next platform lock-in will not be enforced by contracts or APIs but by defaults inside the agent layer — which model gets called, which tool wins ties, whose context takes precedence — and the only durable countermeasure is structural: exportable context and third-party-contestable routing, designed in before the layer consolidates.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Default Routing Is the New Browser Bundling

article_ideas.angle: Reframe 'internal agent' from a prompt-engineering project into an infrastructure ownership problem, with a concrete failure taxonomy: stale context, unauthorized context, and unattributable context.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise platform teams and CTOs scoping internal agent programs
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise agent quality is bounded by the governance of the corpus the agent reads, not by the model behind it; teams that budget for ingestion pipelines, per-document ACLs, staleness detection, and citation as first-class production systems will outperform teams that keep buying better models against an ungoverned index.
article_ideas.title: The Company Brain Is a Maintenance Contract, Not a Model Upgrade

article_ideas.angle: Use the ten-podcasts-in-fifteen-minutes example as a design brief for harness requirements: checkpointed intermediate artifacts, cost/context budgeting, and sampling tools for verification at scale.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers designing agent runtimes and evaluation harnesses
article_ideas.thesis: The value-demonstrating agent workflow is fan-out ingestion plus chunked extraction plus aggregation over whole corpora, not turn-by-turn conversation — and building for chat first optimizes the wrong axis (per-turn latency) while ignoring the right ones (extraction fidelity, context budget, and spot-checkability of silent errors).
article_ideas.title: Stop Building Chat: The Real Runtime Shape of Agent Work Is Batch Extraction

article_ideas.angle: Take the two-to-three-year autonomy prediction seriously as a requirements document and derive the minimum viable control surface: action budgets, reversibility classes, and escalation triggers.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and safety-minded builders shipping agentic products
article_ideas.thesis: The predicted shift to agents acting without per-action confirmation is not resolved by making models more trustworthy but by making side effects scoped, budgeted, and reversible — so the engineering agenda for autonomous agents is capability scoping and rollback, and approval gates should be treated as exceptions with explicit cost, not the default safety story.
article_ideas.title: Autonomy Is a Budget Question, Not a Trust Question

connections.relationship: The organizational agent's usefulness depends on permissioned, fresh retrieval over internal corpora, making ACL-aware retrieval a prerequisite rather than an add-on.
Owning the context-and-dispatch layer reproduces platform lock-in dynamics one abstraction level up.

connections.connects_to: evaluation harness design under fixed budgets
connections.relationship: Both use enforced budgets plus a forced decision to maximize judgment signal per unit of review.
Whole-corpus extraction is a pipeline shape (fan-out extraction, then aggregation) rather than a single prompt.

connections.connects_to: agent tool routing and default model selection
connections.relationship: Default routing inside an agent layer is where structural self-preference would manifest technically.

evidence_quotes.text: Straylight, YC's internal AI agent with company brain context.

core_insights.generalization: Any agent that must act competently inside an organization needs a governed context layer (ingestion, ACLs, freshness, provenance) rather than per-session prompt stuffing; the context layer, not the model, determines ceiling on usefulness.
core_insights.insight: An internal agent grounded in a shared organizational corpus ("company brain") is treated as the practical form factor for enterprise agents — the differentiator is not the model but ownership of institutional context that individual chat sessions never accumulate.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It relocates the hard engineering problem from prompting to maintaining a permissioned, fresh, org-wide context store that an agent can query and act on; that store becomes the asset and the failure surface.

evidence_quotes.text: AI is much more than chat; AI agents have massive working memory and context.
AI agents will act like personal operating systems, creating the next browser war.

core_insights.generalization: Each platform shift moves the chokepoint down a layer: whoever owns the context/session abstraction that all tools are called through captures the ecosystem, so portability primitives at that layer are the countermeasure.
core_insights.insight: The stated end-state is the agent as a personal operating system rather than a chat box: it holds the user's context and dispatches work, which makes the agent layer — not the application — the place where switching costs and distribution accrue ("the next browser war").
core_insights.why_it_matters: If the agent layer owns context and mediates tool calls, app-level lock-in weakens and agent-level lock-in strengthens; that changes where to invest defensively (portable memory, export formats, permission models) and where competitive risk comes from.

evidence_quotes.text: AI reading 1,000 pages of text and transcribing podcasts line-by-line.
Garry Tan used an LLM to transcribe and extract themes from his top 10 podcasts in 15 minutes before the interview.

core_insights.generalization: Agent harnesses should support long-running, high-context batch jobs with intermediate artifacts and spot-checkable outputs; the engineering question becomes extraction fidelity versus context length and cost, which is directly benchmarkable.
core_insights.insight: The demonstrated workflow is batch, long-context synthesis — ingesting very large documents and producing structured extraction in minutes — rather than iterative chat; the agent's value shows up in whole-corpus processing, not turn-by-turn assistance.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It points to a different runtime shape: fan-out ingestion, chunk-level extraction, then aggregation/theme clustering, with cost and fidelity dominated by context volume rather than latency per turn.

evidence_quotes.text: 10 minutes is a wonderful constraint, kind of like how 140 characters for Twitter way back in the day was a wonderful constraint.
Paul Graham realized that 10 minutes is the ideal constraint to judge a founder's capability.

core_insights.generalization: Evaluation and screening protocols should be designed around tight, enforced budgets (time, tokens, number of probes) and a forced binary output; the budget is a parameter to tune for signal quality, not an inefficiency to eliminate.
core_insights.insight: A hard, tiny decision budget (10 minutes) is framed as producing better judgments than unbounded deliberation, by analogy to the 140-character constraint — constraint as a signal-forcing device rather than a compromise.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It is a design principle transferable to evaluation harnesses and human-in-the-loop review: fixed, aggressive budgets force decision-relevant questions and suppress diffuse, unfalsifiable discussion.

evidence_quotes.text: Closed platforms and self-preferencing by dominant tech giants can starve the ecosystem of new startups.
Delaware C-Corp governance and Delaware law require maximizing shareholder value, sometimes leading to closed platforms.

core_insights.generalization: Platform-adjacent agent infrastructure should be evaluated on whether routing, defaults, and permissions are contestable by third parties; governance incentives predict gradual closure even absent bad intent.
core_insights.insight: Self-preferencing by the owner of a dominant platform is identified as a structural mechanism that starves the adjacent ecosystem, and the incentive is attributed to corporate-governance duty to maximize shareholder value rather than to malice.
core_insights.why_it_matters: For agent ecosystems, whoever owns the agent layer can privilege its own tools and models; the risk is architectural (default routing, permission precedence) rather than a policy violation, so mitigations must be structural — open protocols, portable context, enforced neutrality.

evidence_quotes.text: Straylight, YC's internal AI agent with company brain context.
AI is much more than chat; AI agents have massive working memory and context.

deep_dives.research_question: For an internal agent grounded in an organization-wide corpus, what fraction of wrong answers is attributable to stale, unauthorized, or unattributed context — and does enforcing per-document ACLs at retrieval time plus freshness metadata reduce that error rate enough to justify the ingestion cost?
deep_dives.topic: The company-brain maintenance contract: ACL-aware retrieval, freshness, and provenance as the real agent substrate
deep_dives.why: Pass 1 relocates difficulty from prompting to the governed context store, but the summary names the artifact ('company brain') with zero operational detail: no ingestion cadence, no staleness detection, no permission enforcement, no citation. Without a measured failure taxonomy, teams will keep tuning models against a broken context layer and misattribute the resulting errors.

evidence_quotes.text: AI reading 1,000 pages of text and transcribing podcasts line-by-line.
Garry Tan used an LLM to transcribe and extract themes from his top 10 podcasts in 15 minutes before the interview.

deep_dives.research_question: At what input length does single-pass whole-corpus extraction lose theme-extraction accuracy relative to fan-out chunk-then-aggregate, and how does total token cost trade against that accuracy gap?
deep_dives.topic: Extraction fidelity as a function of context length and chunking strategy
deep_dives.why: The only demonstrated workflow in the talk is batch synthesis over very large inputs (1,000 pages, ten podcasts, 15 minutes). That is a benchmarkable engineering question — fidelity vs context volume vs cost — yet the evidence given is anecdotal with no human ground truth. Answering it determines the default runtime shape for long-context agent jobs.

evidence_quotes.text: Closed platforms and self-preferencing by dominant tech giants can starve the ecosystem of new startups.
AI agents will act like personal operating systems, creating the next browser war.

deep_dives.research_question: In emerging agent platforms, can a third party contest the default tool routing and model selection, and is accumulated user context exportable in a form that preserves meaning?
deep_dives.topic: Contestability of the agent layer: auditing default routing, permission precedence, and context export
deep_dives.why: If the agent layer becomes the chokepoint that mediates all tool calls, self-preference does not require bad intent — it shows up as defaults and permission precedence. Making that measurable (routing neutrality, export completeness) converts a political worry into an auditable engineering property.

evidence_quotes.text: 10 minutes is a wonderful constraint, kind of like how 140 characters for Twitter way back in the day was a wonderful constraint.
Paul Graham realized that 10 minutes is the ideal constraint to judge a founder's capability.

deep_dives.research_question: Does an enforced, aggressive decision budget (time, tokens, number of probes) with a forced binary output improve inter-rater agreement and downstream hit rate compared with unbounded review, or does it systematically select for fast-legible signals?
deep_dives.topic: Hard decision budgets as a tunable parameter for evaluation signal quality
deep_dives.why: The 10-minute interview claim is presented as a practitioner's settled conclusion, but the mechanism — constraint forces decision-relevant questions — is directly testable and transfers to agent evaluation harnesses and human-in-the-loop review design. If it biases toward fast-legible candidates, that is a costly, invisible failure.

open_questions.question: What maintenance contract keeps a "company brain" correct, current, and permission-correct as the corpus changes?
open_questions.research_direction: Prototype a retrieval layer with per-document ACLs and freshness metadata; measure answer error rate attributable to stale or unauthorized context.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary names the artifact but gives no ingestion cadence, staleness detection, ACL enforcement, or provenance mechanism.

open_questions.question: How does extraction fidelity degrade as input length grows, and where should chunk-then-aggregate replace single-pass ingestion?
open_questions.research_direction: Benchmark theme-extraction accuracy and cost across context lengths and chunking strategies using human-labeled transcript sets.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The 1,000-page and 15-minute examples are anecdotal; no accuracy measurement is reported against human ground truth.

open_questions.question: Is the agent layer converging to a closed, self-preferencing platform or to open, contestable protocols?
open_questions.research_direction: Audit default routing, permission precedence, and third-party tool neutrality in emerging agent platforms; track whether context is exportable.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary asserts a "next browser war" but provides only historical analogy, not evidence about current agent-layer governance.

open_questions.question: What is the actual multiplier on knowledge-worker output, and at what point does verification become the binding constraint?
open_questions.research_direction: Run task-level time studies that separately measure generation time, verification time, and rework rate for agent-assisted vs. unassisted work.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The 400x figure is asserted without methodology; output gains and review costs are not separated.

open_questions.question: Does a fixed decision budget improve or bias screening quality compared with unbounded review?
open_questions.research_direction: Evaluate decisions made under enforced time/token budgets vs. open-ended review for consistency, inter-rater agreement, and downstream hit rate.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The 10-minute optimality is attributed to one practitioner's conclusion; no comparative outcome data is presented.

project_ideas.hypothesis: Enforcing per-document ACLs at retrieval time and propagating freshness/provenance metadata reduces agent answer error rate attributable to stale or unauthorized context by a measurable margin versus a flat, ungoverned index over the same corpus.
project_ideas.measurement: Stale-context error rate, unauthorized-context leakage rate, and correct-answer rate for the governed vs ungoverned index; plus retrieval latency overhead introduced by ACL filtering.
project_ideas.name: Governed Company Brain
project_ideas.poc: Ingest a mid-size internal corpus (docs, transcripts, tickets) into two indexes: one flat embedding index, one with per-document ACL tags and last-modified/freshness fields enforced at query time. Run a fixed question set where a known subset of answers depends on recently changed or access-restricted documents; score answers against ground truth with an unauthorized-disclosure and staleness-error rubric.

project_ideas.hypothesis: Theme-extraction accuracy degrades non-linearly with single-pass input length, and a chunk-then-aggregate pipeline matches or beats single-pass accuracy at a lower token cost beyond a measurable context threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Theme recall/precision versus input length and chunk size; tokens consumed per correctly extracted theme; identification of the crossover length where chunking wins on fidelity-per-dollar.
project_ideas.name: Context-Length Fidelity Curve
project_ideas.poc: Take human-labeled podcast transcripts and document sets with ground-truth theme lists. Run extraction under (a) single-pass at increasing context lengths and (b) chunk-then-aggregate at several chunk sizes, then score recall and precision of extracted themes against the labels.

project_ideas.hypothesis: A screening protocol with an enforced hard budget and a forced binary decision produces higher inter-rater agreement and better downstream outcomes than an unbounded review of the same candidates.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-rater agreement between reviewers under each protocol; decision stability under repeated review; downstream hit rate of accepted candidates at a fixed follow-up horizon.
project_ideas.name: Budgeted Screening Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a review harness that enforces a fixed time/token/probe budget and requires a binary output, then run it in parallel with an open-ended review over the same candidate set (founders, inbound leads, or agent outputs). Track decisions and revisit them after outcomes are known.

project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent platforms exhibit measurable default self-preference — their own tools and models are selected at higher rates than quality-matched third-party alternatives — and context export completeness varies systematically across platforms.
project_ideas.measurement: Default-selection share of platform-owned tools versus quality-matched alternatives; number of steps required to override routing; percentage of context recoverable via export.
project_ideas.name: Agent Layer Neutrality Audit
project_ideas.poc: Construct a set of tasks where a third-party tool and the platform's own tool are functionally equivalent and quality-matched. Observe which is routed by default, then test whether routing is overridable and whether accumulated context can be fully exported and re-imported.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Walter Isaacson
  • Channel: The Builders with Walter Isaacson
  • Main topic: Startup culture, venture capital, and the disruptive impact of AI agents on society and tech
  • Purpose: To explore the inner workings of Y Combinator, founder archetypes, and how AI agents and AI-driven operating systems will fundamentally reshape the tech landscape and society. Walter Isaacson interviews Garry Tan, CEO of Y Combinator, discussing founder psychology, YC acceptance rates, the philosophy of venture capital, the antitrust battles in big tech, immigrant contributions to US startup culture, and the impending revolution of AI agents over the next 2 to 3 years.

Topic Map

Y Combinator Selection Process and Founder Psychology

  • Explanation: Discussion on YC's acceptance rates (less than 1%), 10-minute final interviews, and what makes a successful startup founder.
  • Key claims:
    • YC receives 80,000 to 90,000 applications a year for about 800 spots.
    • Paul Graham realized that 10 minutes is the ideal constraint to judge a founder's capability.
    • 10 to 15 percent of all self-made billionaires under 50 are YC alumni.
  • Examples:
    • Elon Musk walking into YC and getting funded instantly in his current form.
    • Garry Tan's startup Simpleton blogs and YC demo.
  • Terminology:
    • Y Combinator
    • self-made billionaires
    • startup founders
  • Why it matters: Shows how strict constraints and rapid evaluations identify transformative founders.

Big Tech, Antitrust, and Open Markets

  • Explanation: Examining whether big tech is too powerful and how antitrust battles impact innovation and startup ecosystems.
  • Key claims:
    • True free-market enterprise has never been tried in tech.
    • Google survived and thrived because of DOJ actions against Microsoft.
    • Monopolies on railroads and browsers stifled competition unless challenged.
  • Examples:
    • Microsoft taking over the browser market via Windows.
    • Google's growth influenced by DOJ consent decrees.
  • Terminology:
    • antitrust
    • monopoly
    • big tech
    • consent decree
  • Why it matters: Highlights the tension between corporate consolidation and open markets for startups.

Immigrants and American Innovation

  • Explanation: The role of immigrant founders in building American technology and YC startups.
  • Key claims:
    • About 50 percent of startups that make it have at least one immigrant co-founder.
    • Immigrants come to America to build the future, reflecting a unique American trait.
  • Examples:
    • Garry Tan's family coming from Burma as refugees and his father from Singapore.
  • Terminology:
    • immigrant co-founders
    • startup culture
    • prosperity
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates that openness to immigration is a core pillar of US tech dominance.

The AI Agent Revolution

  • Explanation: How AI agents will replace chat interfaces and become autonomous personal operating systems within 2 to 3 years.
  • Key claims:
    • AI is much more than chat; AI agents have massive working memory and context.
    • AI agents will act like personal operating systems, creating the next browser war.
    • In 2 to 3 years, everyone will use AI agents autonomously, changing how humans work and live.
  • Examples:
    • Straylight, YC's internal AI agent with company brain context.
    • AI reading 1,000 pages of text and transcribing podcasts line-by-line.
  • Terminology:
    • AI agents
    • LLM
    • working memory
    • browser war
    • operating system
  • Why it matters: Projects the immediate future of human-computer interaction and productivity gains.

Key Points

10-Minute Interviews as a Constraint

  • Explanation: YC evaluates founders in just 10 minutes by focusing on user problems, technology solutions, and founder-market fit.
  • Evidence: Paul Graham discovered that 10 minutes is an optimal constraint to make an up/down decision on founders.
  • Practical implication: Speed and simplicity in evaluation help identify exceptional talent quickly.

The Danger of Big Tech Monopolies

  • Explanation: Closed platforms and self-preferencing by dominant tech giants can starve the ecosystem of new startups.
  • Evidence: Delaware C-Corp governance and Delaware law require maximizing shareholder value, sometimes leading to closed platforms.
  • Practical implication: Regulation and open-source models are needed to prevent market stagnation.

AI Agents as the Next Operating System

  • Explanation: AI is shifting from simple chat interfaces to autonomous agents with vast contextual memory that act on behalf of users.
  • Evidence: AI can now ingest thousands of pages of documents, analyze personal notes, and execute complex workflows autonomously.
  • Practical implication: Every knowledge worker will leverage AI agents to multiply their output by 400x.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

YC 10-Minute Founder Evaluation Framework

  • How it works: Evaluate founders rapidly based on user pain points, technology value, and founder drive.
  • Components:
    • User problem identification
    • Technology solution
    • Founder-market fit
    • 10-minute time constraint
  • When to use: When assessing early-stage startup founders and high-velocity investments.

Examples & Case Studies

Garry Tan pitched YC with simple blogs by email and a strong demo.

  • Illustrates: How clear, immediate value propositions secure funding without lengthy pitches.
  • Lesson: Show a working demo and solve a real problem immediately.

Garry Tan used an LLM to transcribe and extract themes from his top 10 podcasts in 15 minutes before the interview.

  • Illustrates: The practical power of AI agents in daily professional workflows.
  • Lesson: Leverage AI agents to synthesize large volumes of information instantly.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Embrace AI agents to automate data processing and personal workflows.
    • Focus on open-source tools to avoid platform lock-in.
  • Strategic:
    • Maintain open markets and prevent big tech gatekeeping to protect startup innovation.
    • Recognize that AI agents will redefine personal and enterprise computing within 2-3 years.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How will AI agent proliferation impact employment and job displacement?
    • What regulatory frameworks will govern open-source versus proprietary AI models?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • About 50 percent of all startups that make it have at least one immigrant co-founder. (statistical)
  • Microsoft used Windows platform advantage to take over the browser market. (historical)

Notable Quotes

"10 minutes is a wonderful constraint, kind of like how 140 characters for Twitter way back in the day was a wonderful constraint." (at 1:53) "True free-market enterprise has never been tried." (at 15:11) "Everybody wants to tell you how to do it and they never did it." (at 5:53)

Compressed Summary

  • YC evaluates founders in fast 10-minute interviews.
  • Immigrant co-founders drive a massive share of top US startups.
  • AI agents are evolving from chat tools into autonomous personal operating systems.
  • Open markets and anti-monopoly measures are essential for startup survival.
  • Keywords: ai agents, startup culture, venture capital, llm, antitrust
  • Core insight: AI agents will transition from simple chat interfaces to autonomous personal operating systems, fundamentally redefining productivity and tech market competition within two to three years.

- **How it works**: Evaluate founders rapidly based on user pain points, technology value, and founder drive.
- **Components**:
  - User problem identification
  - Technology solution
  - Founder-market fit
  - 10-minute time constraint
- **When to use**: When assessing early-stage startup founders and high-velocity investments.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Garry Tan pitched YC with simple blogs by email and a strong demo.
- **Illustrates**: How clear, immediate value propositions secure funding without lengthy pitches.
- **Lesson**: Show a working demo and solve a real problem immediately.
### Garry Tan used an LLM to transcribe and extract themes from his top 10 podcasts in 15 minutes before the interview.
- **Illustrates**: The practical power of AI agents in daily professional workflows.
- **Lesson**: Leverage AI agents to synthesize large volumes of information instantly.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Embrace AI agents to automate data processing and personal workflows.
  - Focus on open-source tools to avoid platform lock-in.
- **Strategic**:
  - Maintain open markets and prevent big tech gatekeeping to protect startup innovation.
  - Recognize that AI agents will redefine personal and enterprise computing within 2-3 years.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How will AI agent proliferation impact employment and job displacement?
  - What regulatory frameworks will govern open-source versus proprietary AI models?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- About 50 percent of all startups that make it have at least one immigrant co-founder. (statistical)
- Microsoft used Windows platform advantage to take over the browser market. (historical)
## Notable Quotes
> "10 minutes is a wonderful constraint, kind of like how 140 characters for Twitter way back in the day was a wonderful constraint." (at 1:53)
> "True free-market enterprise has never been tried." (at 15:11)
> "Everybody wants to tell you how to do it and they never did it." (at 5:53)
## Compressed Summary
- YC evaluates founders in fast 10-minute interviews.
- Immigrant co-founders drive a massive share of top US startups.
- AI agents are evolving from chat tools into autonomous personal operating systems.
- Open markets and anti-monopoly measures are essential for startup survival.
- **Keywords**: ai agents, startup culture, venture capital, llm, antitrust
- **Core insight**: AI agents will transition from simple chat interfaces to autonomous personal operating systems, fundamentally redefining productivity and tech market competition within two to three years.
